audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2, 5 and 6 read Volibear / Volibear / Volibear / Skill in both layers, while the packet chart gives Wukong / Skill / Wukong / Wukong. The content whys already said 'Level 2 favours Wukong', 'Level 3 returns to skill', 'First item flips to Wukong' and 'the late edge is Wukong's' — so four rows printed a side token contradicting the sentence next to it.
audit.why: Wukong's early burst pattern (Crushing Blow plus the Warrior Trickster clone) beats a level-2 Frenzied Maul trade, level 3 is genuinely even as your stacks start closing the gap, and from first item on his armour shred and Nimbus Strike gap-close win short bursts that Volibear's sustain profile needs a long fight to answer. This matches the 47.93% win rate over 1471 games far better than a chart giving Volibear five of seven rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 5 and 6 set to the packet sides in both layers as one atomic group, ratings moved to 4/10, 5/10, 4/10 and 3/10, and all four full-layer whys rewritten so they stop claiming a Volibear kill window.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why and phases[6].why both handed the item stages to Volibear ('Force Wukong to fight or lose the wave', 'a drain-tank Wukong can't burst'), which inverts the two stages Wukong actually takes.
audit.why: Sundered Sky's heal pays out over an extended fight; Wukong's spike is short-burst with armour shred and a gap-close he can leave on, so he is not obliged to give you that fight. Late, Cyclone plus Nimbus Strike is the stronger fight-starting package, which content late already states.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why now says his first item plus armour shred out-trades you in short bursts; phases[6].why names Cyclone and the gap-close and tells you to close the game before then.

audit.whatIsWrong: The clone-baiting rule — the single most important interaction in this lane — is written with the wrong ability in three places: spikes[1].text, wants.you[1] and content.mid all say to 'E-stun' after the clone pops.
audit.why: Sky Splitter (E, 16s, 1200 range) damages, slows and shields Volibear only when he stands in the blast radius. It has no stun. Thundering Smash (Q, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) is the stun, and because it is an auto-attack reset the stun resolves on the next attack — which is exactly why it can be held through the clone and spent on the real body. Told to press E, the player burns the wrong cooldown and the clone eats nothing.
audit.corrected: All three fields now name the Q stun / Thundering Smash and keep the hold-until-the-clone-pops sequencing.

audit.whatIsWrong: champ-data/_kits/wukong.json was not supplied in this brief (enemyKit is null), so no Wukong cooldowns, ranges or costs could be verified.
audit.why: Every concrete number for his side of the lane — Warrior Trickster's cooldown, Nimbus Strike's cooldown, Cyclone's duration — would have to be asserted without a source, which the run forbids.
audit.corrected: No Wukong cooldown numbers were added anywhere. All rewrites here use only Volibear's verified kit numbers and Wukong's ability names from packet.enemyAbilities.

edits.before: Q + W online — stun in, double-bite out. Wukong has to respect every walk-up once your second W heal-bite threatens.
edits.after: Q + W online, but Crushing Blow and his Warrior Trickster clone win the level-2 burst — trade only after the W is spent.

edits.before: E completes the pattern: shield yourself as you disengage or slow Wukong under the sky-splitter. This is the start of your kill window.
edits.after: Sky Splitter shields you only if you stand in the blast. Frenzied Maul stacks are closing the gap here, but the burst trade is still even.

edits.before: Sundered Sky doubles down on the all-in: crit-heal on the first hit of every fight. Force Wukong to fight or lose the wave.
edits.after: His first item plus armour shred out-trades you in short bursts — Sundered Sky's heal wants a long fight he will not give you.

edits.before: With two items you're a drain-tank Wukong can't burst. Only discipline beats you now — never int the Q stun into ready CC and the lane stays yours.
edits.after: Two items in, Cyclone and the Nimbus Strike gap-close make him the better fighter — group with Stormbringer and close the game before that.

edits.before: Stormbringer's slow and your CC let you all-in through his W clone dodge — E-stun him after the clone pops, not before.
edits.after: Stormbringer's slow lets you all-in through his W clone dodge — hold the Q stun until the clone pops, then land it on the real body.

edits.before: E-stun after his W clone appears
edits.after: Q-stun after his W clone appears

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are yours — Frenzied Maul sustain catches up and Stormbringer lets you all-in through his clone dodge if you time E after it pops.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are yours — Frenzied Maul sustain catches up and Stormbringer lets you all-in through his clone dodge if you time Q after it pops.

notes: No Wukong kit file was included in this brief (enemyKit is null), so nothing on his side carries a cooldown number — I used only his ability names from packet.enemyAbilities and asserted no Wukong timings. Four chart rows were desynced from the packet and from their own why text and are now proposed as matched pairs. Same E-stun error as the vayne and vladimir pages: Sky Splitter has no stun, so 'E-stun after the clone pops' pointed the player at the wrong button on the one beat that decides this lane.
